title: Partial sums and kernel projections for supplied quotient presentations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M\in\mathrm{ModuleCat}^{v}(R)$, and $E$ a linearly ordered type with well-founded strict order, with no universe relation imposed. Let $F_e\subseteq M$ be monotone and exhaustive and let $P(e)$ be supplied projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension] of $F_e/(\sup_{i<e}F_i\cap F_e)$ [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module]. There exist a short exact complex $S$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] with $S_3=M$ and categorically projective $S_2$, and monotone exhaustive submodules $H_e\subseteq S_2$. Put $K_e=S_1\cap H_e$, precisely the inverse image along $S.f$, and $V_e=(\sup_{i<e}K_i)\cap K_e$ viewed as a submodule of $K_e$. For every $e$, either $V_e=K_e$ or there is a surjective $R$-linear map $q_e:K_e\to\ker(P(e)_0\to Q_e)$ whose linear kernel is exactly $V_e$. These maps come from component projections in the active-index direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], not from an asserted quotient isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 0D1U (lemma-colimit-projective-dimension), successor proof: projective presentation, kernel intersections, and exact sequence of successive quotients

proof.text: Obtain the projective middle module B, linear map b, exhaustive monotone H, stage-image equalities and component maps from the component-data construction. The covering hypothesis and b(H_e)=F_e imply that b is surjective. Use Mathlib LinearMap.shortComplexKer and shortExact_shortComplexKer to construct S with S.X3 definitionally M.

For any injective linear map, pulling back a predecessor supremum in a linearly ordered family equals the supremum of the pullbacks. If predecessors exist, use Submodule.mem_iSup_of_directed and monotonicity; otherwise both sides are bottom by injectivity. Apply this to the inclusion of ker b. At an inactive stage, H_e is its predecessor supremum, so the asserted submodule of K_e is top.

At an active stage restrict p_e to K_e. Its image is killed by the supplied augmentation, by the two commuting identities. This gives qlin into the linear augmentation kernel. For a vector y in that kernel, choose x in H_e with p_e(x)=y. The commuting identity makes a_e(x) lie in the predecessor supremum of F. The image under b of the predecessor supremum of H equals that supremum by map_iSup and the stage-image equalities. Choose z in the predecessor supremum with b(z)=b(x). Then x-z belongs to K_e, p_e(z)=0 by the prescribed kernel of p_e, and qlin(x-z)=y. This proves surjectivity.

The kernel of qlin consists precisely of elements whose image in H_e lies in ker p_e, hence in the predecessor supremum of H. The pullback identity already proved identifies it with the predecessor supremum of K, pulled back to K_e. Transport qlin through ModuleCat.kernelIsoKer.symm.toLinearEquiv to the categorical augmentation kernel. Surjectivity and the kernel equality are preserved by this equivalence.

theorem exists_projective_presentation_kernel_projection_data
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (M : ModuleCat.{v} R)
    {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E] [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)]
    (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
    (P : ∀ e : E, ProjectiveResolution
      (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
        ((⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, F i.val).comap (F e).subtype)))) :
    ∃ S : ShortComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R), S.X₃ = M ∧ S.ShortExact ∧
      Projective S.X₂ ∧ ∃ H : E → Submodule R S.X₂,
        Monotone H ∧ (∀ x : S.X₂, ∃ e : E, x ∈ H e) ∧
        ∀ e : E,
          let K : E → Submodule R S.X₁ := fun i ↦ (H i).comap S.f.hom
          let U := (⨆ i : {j : E // j < e}, K i.val).comap (K e).subtype
          U = ⊤ ∨ ∃ q : K e →ₗ[R] (kernel ((P e).π.f 0) : ModuleCat.{v} R),
            Function.Surjective q ∧ q.ker = U
